sources.citation: Beech, Mervyn W. H. 1908. The Tidong dialects of Borneo (with a grammatical Appendix by A. A. Fokker). Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For the TARAKAN and BOLONGAN dialects (= Southern Tidung sout3241 and Bulungan, not Northern Tidung): p.19 'For the pronunciation of words a general rule can be made that the accent falls on the penultimate, as in Malay, Dayak, Javanese, Sundanese, &c.'; Fokker's Appendix sec. 7 p.109 'Accent. The general rule is: the accent lies on the penult, provided this does not contain e [e muet]' with examples, sec. 8 pp.109-110 suffixes shift accent to the new penult if the word ends in a vowel.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2015. Change Request 2015-058 (J. Lobel): split Tidong [tid] into Tidung, Northern [ntd] and Tidung, Southern [itd]; with new-code request forms for ntd and itd.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; defines Northern Tidung as Sabah-only (Beluran, Sandakan, Tawau districts), c. 5,000 speakers, retaining Philippine-type voice morphology; Southern Tidung = Kalabakan + Kalimantan Utara.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. http://hdl.handle.net/10125/101972
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress rule stated for any Tidung variety. But fn.2 p.196 defines the diacritics used 'throughout this dissertation' (acute = stressed vowel; circumflex = stressed final vowel + glottal stop), and the first-hand Tidung Bangawong-Labuk (= Northern Tidung) sentences in examples (24)-(33), pp.167-170, and p.178 carry these marks overwhelmingly on the FINAL syllable (makow', ontudu'ng, taka'w, suwa'b, ingga'y, inumo'n, tulungo'n, tokowo'n, takawa'n, natakawa'n, nadatu', datu^, sumila^, antako'w), with a handful of penults on pronouns/adverbs (doda'noy, dosi'yo, da'mon). Implicit evidence only.
